title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
gist: DoorDash replaced its monolithic dispatch optimization engine — whose roughly quadratic algorithms faced peak demand near four times capacity — with a stateful-coordinator / stateless-worker architecture using gRPC payload sharding and hierarchical geographic decomposition, achieving 10x throughput, >99.99% availability on Super Bowl Sunday, and in-path ML and multi-agent reinforcement learning.

insights.claim: DoorDash's legacy dispatch engine tightly coupled business logic, logistics state and routing algorithms with roughly quadratic time complexity, and at peak demand approached four times its processing capacity, forcing fallback heuristics and assignments on incomplete information.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows how logistics marketplaces hit algorithmic, not just hardware, scaling walls as volume grows.
insights.quote: The fatal bottleneck wasn't just raw machine capacity; it was the speed of reality.
insights.locator: The previous dispatch engine tightly coupled

insights.claim: DoorDash chose a new execution model over conventional horizontal scaling to fix its dispatch bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Architecture redesign, not more servers, was the lever — relevant to judging infra spend efficiency.
insights.quote: the system didn't just need more capacity; it demanded a fundamentally new execution model.
insights.locator: Rather than address the bottleneck through conventional horizontal scaling

insights.claim: DoorDash's new dispatch platform splits into a stateful coordinator managing dispatch lifecycles, global logistics state and business rules, and stateless compute workers handling optimization, vehicle-routing heuristics and model inference, each scaling independently.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Separating coordination from computation is a reusable pattern for real-time optimization systems.
insights.locator: The new platform separates execution into two independently scalable tiers

insights.claim: DoorDash's coordinator sends only localized logistics data to workers via payload sharding over gRPC and partitions the problem into geographic clusters and delivery trajectories, with a reconciliation layer merging partition results.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Hierarchical decomposition turns a global optimization into parallelizable subproblems, cutting network overhead.
insights.locator: The coordinator distributes localized portions of logistics data

insights.claim: DoorDash validated the new dispatch platform with shadow testing on duplicated production requests, comparing matching quality, delivery times and resilience to the legacy engine, then rolled out with switchback experiments and fallback mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Low-risk migration practice for mission-critical marketplace systems.

insights.claim: DoorDash reports a tenfold increase in dispatch throughput with more than 99.96% of runs completing within 20 seconds, and more than 99.99% availability on Super Bowl Sunday despite a 10% week-over-week rise in peak volume.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Dispatch headroom supports DoorDash's ability to absorb demand growth without degrading delivery quality.

themes.theme: ML and RL in the dispatch path

insights.claim: DoorDash uses hybrid L1/L2 model serving: latency-sensitive inference runs locally in compute workers via ONNX Runtime to avoid RPC overhead, while heavier evaluations go to isolated remote model-serving clusters.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Pattern for embedding ML inference in latency-critical paths without centralized serving bottlenecks.
insights.locator: The architecture also introduces a hybrid L1/L2 model serving

insights.claim: DoorDash deploys multi-agent reinforcement learning to adjust dispatch objective weights per store based on merchant congestion and courier utilization, trading off delivery speed against batching efficiency; the approach was validated in production switchback experiments and accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Reinforcement Learning from World Feedback.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Production RL for marketplace optimization could improve courier efficiency and unit economics.
insights.locator: DoorDash has also deployed multi-agent reinforcement learning
